_meta.indication: RYTELO is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with low- to intermediate-1 risk MDS with transfusion-dependent anemia requiring 4 or more RBC units over 8 weeks who have not responded to or have lost response to or are ineligible for ESA.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial; imetelstat 7.1 mg/kg IV every 4 weeks vs matching placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with low- to intermediate-1 risk MDS with transfusion-dependent anemia requiring 4 or more RBC units over 8 weeks who failed to respond to, lost response to, or are ineligible for ESA treatment.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: rate of 8-week RBC transfusion independence (RBC-TI).
pivotal_trials.n: N=178 enrolled; participants randomized 2:1 to RYTELO (n=118) or placebo (n=60).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (including lab abnormalities) were decreased platelets, decreased white blood cells, decreased neutrophils, increased AST/ALP/ALT, fatigue, prolonged PTT, arthralgia/myalgia, COVID-19, and headache. Grade 3/4 decreased platelets occurred in 65% and Grade 3/4 decreased neutrophils in 72% of patients treated with RYTELO.
target_moa: Imetelstat is a specific inhibitor of human telomerase; a 13-mer thio-phosphoramidate oligonucleotide that binds the template region of the RNA component of human telomerase (hTR), inhibiting telomerase enzymatic activity and preventing telomere binding.
modality: Oligonucleotide (small molecule 13-mer thio-phosphoramidate oligonucleotide telomerase inhibitor).

advisory_committee.vote: ODAC met 3/14/2024; voted Yes 12, No 2, Abstain 0 that imetelstat's benefits outweigh its risks.

basis.text: Fast Track Designation granted October 27, 2017 for transfusion-dependent anemia due to low or intermediate-1 risk MDS not associated with del(5q) and refractory or resistant to ESA.

citations.quote: On October 27, 2017, imetelstat was granted fast track designation for the treatment of adult patients with transfusion-dependent anemia due to low or intermediate-1 risk MDS that is not associated with the del5q abnormality and who are refractory or resistant to treatment with an ESA.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation granted December 23, 2015 for the treatment of patients with MDS.

citations.quote: On December 23, 2015, imetelstat was granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of patients with MDS.

summary.text: RYTELO received regular (traditional) approval as a standard review NME NDA. Imetelstat held Orphan Drug Designation (2015) and Fast Track Designation (2017) for MDS; an ODAC meeting was convened before approval. It was not an accelerated approval.

requirement.text: 4631-5 To potentially minimize the serious risks of imetelstat treatment including neutropenia and thrombocytopenia and other serious adverse events and improve tolerability, conduct a randomized trial comparing at least 2 dosages of imetelstat in patients with low or intermediate-1 risk myelodysplastic syndromes (LR-MDS) to evaluate alternative dosing regimens such as different dose levels, dosing frequencies, and duration of treatment.

citations.quote: 4631-5 To potentially minimize the serious risks of imetelstat treatment including neutropenia and thrombocytopenia and other serious adverse events and improve tolerability, conduct a randomized trial comparing at least 2 dosages of imetelstat in patients with low or intermediate-1 risk myelodysplastic syndromes (LR-MDS) to evaluate alternative dosing regimens such as different dose levels, dosing frequencies, and duration of treatment. The study should include sufficient clinical pharmacokinetic sampling to analyze the exposure-response (ER) relationships. Update the current population pharmacokinetics (PopPK) and ER analysis with this clinical trial data. The trial should enroll sufficient representation of U.S. racial and ethnic minorities to ensure that the results are reflective of the U.S. population. Additionally, the study should follow subjects for a sufficient time after end of dosing to establish the time required to return to baseline grade for neutrophil and platelet count, in the absence of disease progression or subsequent therapy.
